name: Mode
tip: Instrument plays the loaded sample with MIDI. FX works on the audio passing through the track.

name: Capture
tip: How many seconds of the incoming audio Hairball keeps ready to freeze (FX mode).

name: Freeze
tip: FX mode: stop recording and keep looping what is in the buffer. Grains then play only the frozen audio.

name: Hold
tip: Holds the playing position still, like Wave Spacing at 0 for a moment. Automate it for stutters and stalls.

name: Lag
tip: FX mode, not frozen: how far behind the live audio the grains read.

name: Attack
tip: Fade in and fade out of each grain. Added to the grain length on both ends.

name: Hold len
tip: Length each grain plays before the next one takes over.

name: Gr. spacing
tip: Gap between grains. 100 percent places them end to end with a clean crossfade. Lower means more overlap and a thicker sound, higher means gaps.

name: Wave spacing
tip: How fast the playing position moves through the sound. 100 is normal, 0 freezes, negative plays the grains backwards in order, 300 is three times faster.

name: Pan
tip: Odd grains go left, even grains go right. 0 is off.

name: Depth
tip: Size of the LFO that moves Wave spacing. 0 is off.

name: Speed
tip: Speed of the LFO on Wave spacing.

name: Rand
tip: Randomises where each grain starts, so the order is shuffled. 0 is off.

name: Transients
tip: Grains that cross a hit snap to it and take the Transient length. Off, Regions (slices you provide) or Detect (automatic).

name: Trans. len
tip: Length of grains that start on a transient.

name: Loop
tip: Loop the sound when the position reaches the end.

name: Key to
tip: What the MIDI keys do: Pitch, Percent (C5 to C7 pick the start position), Step (C5 and up offset the start by steps), Transient (C5 and up pick a slice).

name: Start
tip: Where in the sound playing starts.

name: Root key
tip: The MIDI note that plays the sound at its original pitch.

name: Pitch
tip: Pitch in semitones. Grains are read faster or slower; the position still moves at Wave spacing.

name: Fine
tip: Fine tune in cents.

name: Env amt
tip: Pitch envelope. Starts this many semitones away from the pitch and glides back to it.

name: Env time
tip: How long the pitch envelope takes to return to the set pitch.

name: Env curve
tip: Shape of the pitch envelope. Below 1 snaps back fast, above 1 lingers away from the pitch.

name: Glide
tip: Instrument: time to slide between notes.

name: Riser
tip: Starts the riser. In Instrument mode every note starts it. Turn it off and it eases back.

name: Time
tip: How long the riser takes to reach its end.

name: Curve
tip: Below 1 jumps up early, above 1 builds slowly and shoots up at the end.

name: Pitch up
tip: How many semitones the riser lifts the pitch.

name: Grains
tip: How far the grains shrink and speed up as the riser builds.

name: Tone
tip: Grains get so close they turn into a pitched tone at the Tone Hz (or the key you play). 0 stays granular.

name: Tone Hz
tip: Pitch the grains settle on at the top of the riser (FX mode).

name: Filter up
tip: Opens the filter by this many octaves while the riser builds.

name: Follow key
tip: Instrument: the riser tone follows the key you play.

name: Attack
tip: Instrument: note fade in.

name: Decay
tip: Instrument: fall to the sustain level.

name: Sustain
tip: Instrument: level while the key is held.

name: Release
tip: Instrument: note fade out.

name: Voices
tip: Instrument: how many notes can play at once. Fewer voices use less CPU.

name: Width
tip: Mid/side width. 100 is unchanged, 0 is mono, 200 is double the side signal.

name: Bass mono
tip: Keeps everything below this frequency in the middle. 0 is off.

name: Low
tip: Low shelf at 120 Hz.

name: Mid
tip: Bell filter gain.

name: Mid Hz
tip: Bell filter frequency.

name: Mid Q
tip: Bell filter width. Higher is narrower.

name: High
tip: High shelf at 8 kHz.

name: Filter
tip: Off, Low pass, High pass or Band pass.

name: Cutoff
tip: Filter cutoff. The riser can open it by itself.

name: Reso
tip: Filter resonance.

name: Drive
tip: Symmetric analog clip. Odd harmonics, loud and bright. Above 100 percent needs Nasty range.

name: Transistor
tip: Neve style asymmetric stage. Even harmonics, warm and thick. Above 100 percent needs Nasty range.

name: Fuzz
tip: Lopsided hard fuzz. Above 80 percent it turns nasty on purpose. Above 100 percent needs Nasty range.

name: Dance
tip: Glue compressor on everything above 150 Hz, bass left alone. Pumps and holds the sound together for dance music.

name: Dry/wet
tip: Blend between the untouched input and Hairball. At 0 the input passes bit for bit.

name: Output
tip: Output level.

name: Limiter
tip: Safety limiter at the output, never above 0 dBFS.

name: Nasty range
tip: Lets Drive, Transistor and Fuzz go beyond 100 percent. Off by default.
